$$g(\ell,\ell)=g(v_0,v_0)+g(v_0,v_0)g(v_0,k)+\frac14g(v_0,v_0)^2g(k,k)=0,$$
since $g(v_0,k)=-1$ and $g(k,k)=0$. This construction is smooth locally and gives a null field $\ell$ paired with $k$ by $-1$.

Let $P_p:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{k_p,\ell_p\}$. Its Gram matrix in the ordered basis $(k_p,\ell_p)$ is $\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$, with determinant $-1$ and eigenvalues $1,-1$, so it is nondegenerate with inertia $(1,1,0)$. Every $X\in k_p^\perp$ has a unique decomposition $X=a k_p+b\ell_p+z$ with $z\in P_p^\perp$. Pairing with $k_p$ gives $0=g(k_p,X)=-b$, so $b=0$. Hence $k_p^\perp=\mathbb Rk_p\oplus P_p^\perp$, and the quotient map restricts to a linear isomorphism from $P_p^\perp$ to $\mathcal S_p$. Changing a representative by a multiple of $k_p$ does not change $g_p(X,Y)$ because every representative lies in $k_p^\perp$; under the isomorphism the quotient form is the positive-definite restriction to $P_p^\perp$ from step 2.1. derivations.claim: On $\mathbb R^{1,3}\setminus\{x=0\}$ put $r=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2}$, $n_i=x_i/r$, $H=\{t+r=0,\ r>0\}$, and $k=\partial_t-\sum_i n_i\partial_{x_i}$. By [F6], $r$ is smooth for $r>0$, so $H$ is a smooth embedded hypersurface. Its normal covector is $d(t+r)=dt+dr$, whose Minkowski dual is $-\partial_t+\partial_r=-k$ and whose squared norm is zero; hence $H$ is null and $k$ is a future null normal tangent to $H$.

The components of the Minkowski metric are constant in the global Cartesian chart, so [F4]'s Christoffel formula gives zero Christoffel symbols. The coordinate curvature formula in [F2] then gives $R^a{}_{bcd}=0$ and hence $\operatorname{Ric}(k,k)=0$. Also $k(r)=-1$ and $k(n_i)=k(x_i/r)=(-n_i r+x_i)/r^2=0$, so the Cartesian components of $k$ are constant along each integral curve and $\nabla_k k=0$. Thus the generator parameter $\lambda=t$ is affine and $r(\lambda)=r_0-(\lambda-\lambda_0)$ until the vertex.

Each cut $S_\lambda:=\{t=\lambda,\ r=r(\lambda)\}$ is a round two-sphere of radius $r(\lambda)>0$ with induced metric $r(\lambda)^2(d\vartheta^2+\sin^2\vartheta\,d\varphi^2)$ and area $A(\lambda)=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi r(\lambda)^2\sin\vartheta\,d\vartheta\,d\varphi=4\pi r(\lambda)^2$. In a screen-orthonormal basis, for any screen vector $X$ one has $\nabla_X k=-X(n_i)\partial_{x_i}=-X/r$, because $X(r)=0$ and $X(x_i)=X_i$; hence $B=-\bar g/r$, $\theta=-2/r$, and directly $A'(\lambda)=-8\pi r(\lambda)<0$.

At the finite future parameter $\lambda_*=\lambda_0+r_0$, every generator from the initial sphere reaches the common vertex $r=0$. The cone ceases to be a smooth embedded null hypersurface there and the flow map collapses the two-sphere to one point, so the future-persistent embedded-cut hypothesis [F5] fails. The strict area decrease on each smooth pre-vertex interval therefore refutes the stated weaker claim without contradicting [[thm-tgr-smooth-null-area]].
